cards.claim: The authors propose the Transformer, a model architecture that relies entirely on attention mechanisms and eschews recurrence.
cards.evidence_quote: In this work we propose the Transformer, a model architecture eschewing recurrence and instead relying entirely on an attention mechanism to draw global dependencies between input and output.

cards.claim: The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization compared to recurrent models.
cards.evidence_quote: The Transformer allows for significantly more parallelization and can reach a new state of the art in translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.

cards.claim: Recurrent models inherently preclude parallelization within training examples due to their sequential nature.
cards.evidence_quote: This inherently sequential nature precludes parallelization within training examples, which becomes critical at longer sequence lengths

cards.claim: The Transformer reaches a new state of the art in translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.
cards.evidence_quote: can reach a new state of the art in translation quality after being trained for as little as twelve hours on eight P100 GPUs.

cards.claim: The Transformer reduces the number of operations to relate distant positions to a constant number, unlike convolutional models where complexity grows with distance.
cards.evidence_quote: In the Transformer this is reduced to a constant number of operations

cards.claim: Self-attention relates different positions within a single sequence to compute a representation of that sequence.
cards.evidence_quote: Self-attention, sometimes called intra-attention is an attention mechanism relating different positions of a single sequence

cards.claim: The Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention without using sequence-aligned RNNs or convolution.
cards.evidence_quote: the Transformer is the first transduction model relying entirely on self-attention to compute representations

cards.claim: A limitation of the Transformer's approach is reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions.
cards.evidence_quote: at the cost of reduced effective resolution due to averaging attention-weighted positions

cards.claim: The Transformer model utilizes a stacked self-attention and point-wise fully connected layer architecture for both its encoder and decoder components.
cards.evidence_quote: The Transformer follows this overall architecture using stacked self-attention and point-wise, fully connected layers for both the encoder and decoder

cards.claim: The encoder consists of a stack of six identical layers, each containing a multi-head self-attention mechanism and a position-wise feed-forward network with residual connections.
cards.evidence_quote: The encoder is composed of a stack of N = 6 identical layers. Each layer has two sub-layers. The first is a multi-head self-attention mechanism

cards.claim: Scaled Dot-Product Attention computes weights by taking the dot product of queries and keys, scaling them by the square root of the key dimension, and applying softmax.
cards.evidence_quote: We compute the dot products of the query with all keys, divide each by √dk, and apply a softmax function to obtain the weights on the values.

cards.claim: Multi-head attention allows the model to attend to information from different representation subspaces simultaneously by projecting queries, keys, and values multiple times.
cards.evidence_quote: Multi-head attention allows the model to jointly attend to information from different representation subspaces at different positions.

cards.claim: The proposed model relies entirely on attention mechanisms, discarding recurrence and convolutions used in previous sequence transduction models.
cards.evidence_quote: Since our model contains no recurrence and no convolution, in order for the model to make use of the order of the sequence...

cards.claim: The encoder utilizes self-attention layers where keys, values, and queries originate from the same source.
cards.evidence_quote: The encoder contains self-attention layers. In a self-attention layer all of the keys, values and queries come from the same place

cards.claim: Decoder self-attention is masked to prevent leftward information flow, preserving the auto-regressive property.

cards.claim: Positional encodings using sine and cosine functions are added to input embeddings to inject sequence order information.
cards.evidence_quote: To this end, we add "positional encodings" to the input embeddings at the bottoms of the encoder and decoder stacks.

cards.claim: Self-attention layers connect all positions with a constant number of sequential operations, enabling greater parallelization compared to recurrent layers which require O(n) sequential steps.
cards.evidence_quote: a self-attention layer connects all positions with a constant number of sequentially executed operations, whereas a recurrent layer requires O(n) sequential operations.

cards.claim: Self-attention layers are computationally faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length is smaller than the representation dimensionality, which is common in machine translation.
cards.evidence_quote: self-attention layers are faster than recurrent layers when the sequence length n is smaller than the representation dimensionality d

cards.claim: Self-attention allows for shorter path lengths between input and output positions compared to convolutional stacks, facilitating the learning of long-range dependencies.
cards.evidence_quote: The shorter these paths between any combination of positions in the input and output sequences, the easier it is to learn long-range dependencies

cards.claim: Self-attention models can be more interpretable as attention heads often learn to perform tasks related to syntactic and semantic structure.
cards.evidence_quote: many appear to exhibit behavior related to the syntactic and semantic structure of the sentences.

cards.claim: The Transformer (base model) achieves a BLEU score of 27.3 on English-to-German translation with significantly lower training cost compared to previous state-of-the-art models.

cards.evidence_quote: We trained on the standard WMT 2014 English-German dataset consisting of about 4.5 million sentence pairs.

cards.evidence_quote: The big models were trained for 300,000 steps (3.5 days).

cards.claim: The big Transformer model achieves a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4 on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, outperforming previous models by more than 2.0 BLEU.
cards.evidence_quote: the big transformer model (Transformer (big) in Table 2) outperforms the best previously reported models (including ensembles) by more than 2.0 BLEU, establishing a new state-of-the-art BLEU score of 28.4.

cards.claim: On the WMT 2014 English-to-French translation task, the big Transformer model achieves a BLEU score of 41.0 while using less than one-quarter of the training cost of the previous state-of-the-art model.
cards.evidence_quote: our big model achieves a BLEU score of 41.0, outperforming all of the previously published single models, at less than 1/4 the training cost of the previous state-of-the-art model.

cards.claim: Reducing the attention key size dk hurts model quality, suggesting that determining compatibility is difficult and a more sophisticated function than dot product may be beneficial.
cards.evidence_quote: we observe that reducing the attention key size dk hurts model quality. This suggests that determining compatibility is not easy and that a more sophisticated compatibility function than dot product may be beneficial.

cards.claim: The Transformer outperforms the Berkeley-Parser even when trained on a small dataset of 40K sentences.

cards.claim: The Transformer is the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing recurrent layers with multi-headed self-attention.
cards.evidence_quote: we presented the Transformer, the first sequence transduction model based entirely on attention, replacing the recurrent layers most commonly used in encoder-decoder architectures with multi-headed self-attention.

cards.claim: The Transformer achieves new state-of-the-art results on WMT 2014 English-to-German and English-to-French translation tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: On both WMT 2014 English-to-German and WMT 2014 English-to-French translation tasks, we achieve a new state of the art.

cards.claim: The Transformer can be trained significantly faster than architectures based on recurrent or convolutional layers for translation tasks.
cards.evidence_quote: For translation tasks, the Transformer can be trained significantly faster than architectures based on recurrent or convolutional layers.

cards.claim: Future work includes extending the Transformer to other modalities like images and audio, investigating local attention mechanisms, and making generation less sequential.
